title: Diagnosing deceivingly cold dusty galaxies at 3.5 < z < 6: A substantial population of compact starbursts with high infrared optical depths
question: What are the spectroscopic redshifts, ISM properties, and dust optical depths of six seemingly cold dusty galaxies selected as z_phot > 6 candidates, and are their apparently cold dust temperatures caused by high far-infrared optical depths and CMB effects?

data.bands: Band 3 (3mm), Band 6 (1mm / 1.2mm), Band 7 (870 um), and ACA 630 um
data.arrays: ALMA 12m array and ACA (Atacama Compact Array)
data.angular_resolution: ALMA 3mm beam for ID9316: 0.41'' x 0.36''; NOEMA 3mm beams: 1.6'' x 1.1'' to 5.7'' x 4.3''

what.value: COSMOS super-deblended catalog FIR/(sub)mm photometry and radio catalog IDs

evidence.quote: Among the five COMSOS sources, ID3117, 5340, 6309, and 7549 were selected from the COSMOS super-deblended catalog (cite: Jin2018cosmos).
ID12646 was selected from the FIR/(sub)mm super-deblended catalog in the GOODS-North field (cite: Liu2018) as the source with the highest photometric redshift $z_{\rm phot,FIR}\sim6$.

what.value: 1mm and 870 um ALMA photometry for ID9316 from the A3COSMOS catalog

evidence.quote: The 1mm and 870$\mu$m ALMA data of ID9316 were well processed as part of the A$^3$COSMOS catalog (cite: Liu2019A3COSMOS). We therefore directly adopt their measurements.

what.value: Four analogous cold dusty galaxies at z=4-6 merged with the new six-galaxy sample

evidence.quote: These six galaxies are used to extend the original sample of (cite: Jin2019alma) to a total of ten, which is used in the remainder of this paper.

what.value: COSMOS2020 NIR/IRAC photometry (The Farmer and Classic) and S-COSMOS IRAC photometry

evidence.loc: Near-infrared and IRAC photometry and stellar mass
evidence.quote: We cross-matched this sample to the deepest wide-field near-infrared(NIR)/IRAC catalogs from COSMOS2020 (cite: Weaver2021cosmos2020).

evidence.quote: In the right panel of Fig. [6](#Sigma_Td) we also compare with the AS2UDS sample (cite: Stach2019AS2UDS) with quantities calculated by (cite: Gullberg2019) and (cite: Dudzeviciute2020)

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities and extract 3mm spectra and continuum fluxes in uv space
recipe.method: Calibrate ALMA data with observatory CASA script, export to uvfits/uv tables, and extract spectra in uv space with GILDAS (using a fixed Gaussian kernel from continuum for ALMA ID9316, and point-source models at ALMA positions for NOEMA targets)
key_parameters: Gaussian kernel determined from continuum (for ID9316 ALMA); point source model at ALMA positions (for NOEMA)

recipe.goal: Blindly search for emission/absorption lines and measure spectroscopic redshifts and line fluxes
recipe.method: Sweep through full 3 mm continuum-subtracted spectrum using line-search algorithm from Jin et al. (2019)
assumptions: For ID9316 CO(5-4) on the edge of the spectrum, line flux is estimated assuming an identical line profile to CO(4-3)

recipe.goal: Fit FIR/(sub)mm dust SEDs to derive L_IR, beta, T_d, M_d, and lambda_eff
recipe.method: Fit deblended FIR photometry and ALMA/NOEMA continuum fluxes using three MBB setups: (1) optically thin without CMB, (2) optically thin with CMB correction, and (3) optically thick with CMB correction
key_parameters: L_IR integrated over 8-1000 um rest-frame; lambda_eff where optical depth tau = 1
assumptions: Radio data points excluded from fit; SFR = L_IR * 10^-10

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum FWHM sizes and inclination angles in uv space
recipe.method: Fit elliptical models to 870 um and/or 1mm ALMA visibilities in uv space following Puglisi et al. (2019) and Valentino et al. (2020)
key_parameters: R_e is half of the FWHM size; Sigma_SFR = SFR / (2 * pi * R_e^2)

recipe.goal: Measure NIR/IRAC photometry and fit stellar SEDs to derive stellar masses
recipe.method: Cross-match or extract NIR/IRAC photometry using The Farmer with point-like models centered on ALMA positions, then fit stellar SEDs with MICHI2 using BC03 templates and Calzetti attenuation
assumptions: Chabrier (2003) IMF; separate stellar and dust SED fitting without optical-FIR energy balance

recipe.goal: Derive and compare gas masses (from dust, dynamics, and [CI]), SFE, Stefan-Boltzmann limits, and 100 um dust opacity
recipe.method: Compute M_gas,dust via FMR metallicity-dependent G/D ratio; M_gas,dyn from CO line widths, ALMA sizes, inclinations, and stellar masses; M_gas,CI from [CI](1-0) luminosity; and tau_100um = kappa * rho * R_e
key_parameters: Dark matter factor = 0.8 in M_dyn,2Re; 20% uncertainty added to M_gas,dust for metallicity variations; kappa from Jones et al. (2013)
assumptions: T_exc,CI = T_d,thick; spherical geometry for dust volume density rho; high-J CO(4-3) velocity width and 1mm dust continuum size trace the same region

answer_key.quantity: Dust temperature range (optically thin with CMB, five NOEMA sources)
Dust temperature range (optically thick with CMB, all six sources)

evidence.quote: The six sources are well resolved with FWHM sizes in the range of 1.7–3.4 kpc.

evidence.loc: Gas masses from optically thin dust models are overestimated
evidence.quote: We were only able to verify this equivalence for the ALMA 3mm-detected ID9316 in our sample, and find that its CO(4-3) size ($0.39''\pm0.07''$) is in agreement with the dust continuum size (Table 6).

answer_key.quantity: Overestimation factor of dust mass using optically thin fits

evidence.loc: Caution for gas mass estimates based on dust continuum
evidence.quote: The dust masses in this work are overestimated by $2.2\pm0.5$ using optically thin fits

answer_key.quantity: Rest-frame 100 um dust opacity (optically thick case)

evidence.quote: In the optically thick case, as shown by the blue squares, the opacity is systematically lower simply because the dust masses are lower, but it is still high ($0.5<\tau_{\rm 100\mu m}<3.0$ with a median of 1.1).

answer_key.quantity: Lower limit fraction of optically thick dusty galaxies at z~4 (L_IR > 4e12 L_sun)

evidence.quote: We roughly estimated the abundance of galaxies with optically thick dust, which consists of a substantial population (at least 10%) of dusty star-forming galaxies with $L_{\rm IR}>4\times10^{12}~L_{\odot}$ at $z\sim4$.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes, target coordinates, continuum fluxes, line fluxes, sizes, and derived physical parameters are clearly tabulated, and the ALMA data are public. However, 5 of the 6 line scans are from NOEMA, and the exact GILDAS uv-space fitting scripts and MBB SED fitting implementation details are inherited from earlier papers rather than self-contained.
rediscovery_reason: For ID9316 (all-ALMA line scan + continuum) and the ALMA continuum size/flux measurements of ID3117, 5340, 6309, and 7549, all raw data are public in the ALMA archive and the quantitative outputs (z_spec, line fluxes, continuum fluxes, uv sizes, and SED/gas mass parameters) are fully tabulated.
